normalized_requirement: The Ice Class Regulations of 2021 apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 5 July 2021. The provisions in section 1.8 (Ice classes) and chapter 2 (Ice Class Draught) in the 2021 Ice Class Regulations apply to all ships irrespective of their year of build.
The Ice Class Regulations of 2017 apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2019 but before 5 July 2021.
The Ice Class Regulations of 2010 (TRAFI/31298/03.04.01.00/2010) apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2012 but before 1 January 2019.

The Ice Class Regulations of 2008 (8.12.2008 No. 2530/30/2008), issued by the Finnish Maritime Administration, apply to ships contracted for construction on or after 1 January 2010 but before 1 January 2012.

The Ice Class Regulations of 2002 (20.9.2002 No. 5/30/2002), issued by the Finnish Maritime Administration, as amended, apply to ships the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 September 2003 but which have been contracted for construction before 1 January 2010.

The Board of Navigation Rules for Assigning Ships Separate Ice-Due Classes, 1985, (2.9.1985 No. 2575/85/307), as amended, apply to ships the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction on or after 1 November 1986 but before 1 September 2003. On the owner's request, the requirements of the 2008 Ice Class Regulations may, however, be applied to the engine output of such ships.

However, ships of ice class IA Super or IA the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction before 1 September 2003 shall comply with the requirements in section 3.2.2 or 3.2.4 of the Ice Class Regulations of 2017 not later than 1 January in the year when twenty years have elapsed since the year the ship was delivered.

However, ships of ice class IA Super or IA the keels of which have been laid or which have been at a similar stage of construction before 1 September 2003 shall comply with the requirements in section 3.2.2 or 3.2.4 of the Ice Class Regulations of 2017 not later than 1 January in the year when twenty years have elapsed since the year the ship was delivered.
Under section 3 of the Act on the Ice Classes of Ships and Icebreaker Assistance (1121/2005), ships are assigned to ice classes IA Super, IA, IB, IC, II, or III.
The upper ice waterline (UIWL) shall be the envelope of the highest points of the waterlines at which the ship is intended to operate in ice. The line may be a broken line.
The lower ice waterline (LIWL) shall be the envelope of the lowest points of the waterlines at which the ship is intended to operate in ice. The line may be a broken line.

The maximum and minimum ice class draughts at fore and aft perpendiculars shall be determined in accordance with the upper and lower ice waterlines and the draught of the ship at fore and aft perpendiculars, when ice conditions require the ship to be ice-strengthened, shall always be between the upper and lower ice waterlines.

Restrictions on draughts when operating in ice shall be documented and kept on board readily available to the master. The maximum and minimum ice class draughts fore, amidships and aft shall be indicated in the class certificate. For ships built on or after 1 July 2007, if the summer load line in fresh water is anywhere located at a higher level than the UIWL, the ship's sides are to be provided with a warning triangle and with an ice class draught mark at the maximum permissible ice class draught amidships (see Annex III). Ships built before 1 July 2007 shall be provided with such a marking, if the UIWL is below the summer load line, not later than the first scheduled dry docking after 1 July 2007.

The draught and trim, limited by the UIWL, must not be exceeded when the ship is navigating in ice. The salinity of the sea water along the intended route shall be taken into account when loading the ship.

When navigating in ice, draught_amidships_m >= LIWL_draught_amidships_m. Any ballast tank above LIWL that is needed to reach LIWL shall have freezing_prevention_present = true. propeller_highest_point_submerged = true. forward_draught_m >= min((2 + 0.00025*displacement_UIWL_t)*level_ice_thickness_m, 4*level_ice_thickness_m). If multiple UIWL waterlines exist, use the displacement at the greatest-displacement UIWL.

The engine output P is the maximum output the propulsion machinery can continuously deliver to the propeller(s). If the output is restricted by technical means or regulations, P shall be taken as the restricted output.
IF iceClass IN {'IA','IB','IC'}, THEN mcrPower_kW >= max(calculated_required_power_kW, 1000). IF iceClass = 'IA Super', THEN mcrPower_kW >= max(calculated_required_power_kW, 2800).

IF construction_stage_date >= '2003-09-01' AND iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA','IB','IC'}, THEN compute P_min = K_e*(R_CH/1000)^(3/2)/D_p at UIWL and LIWL; use draught-dependent inputs at the corresponding draught, use L and B at UIWL for both calculations, and require mcrPower_kW >= max(P_min_UIWL_kW, P_min_LIWL_kW). K_e shall be selected from Table 3-1. Table 3-1 values for conventional propulsion systems: 1 propeller: CP propeller or electric or hydraulic propulsion machinery 2.03, FP propeller 2.26; 2 propellers: 1.44 and 1.60; 3 propellers: 1.18 and 1.31.

Set C_3 = 845 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_4 = 42 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_5 = 825 kg/s^2 and psi = atan(tan(phi_2)/sin(alpha)). Clamp ((L*T)/B^2)^3 to the inclusive interval [5, 20]. Table 3-2 values: f1=23 N/m2, f2=45.8 N/m, f3=14.7 N/m, f4=29 N/m2, g1=1530 N, g2=170 N/m, g3=400 N/m1.5.

In order to retain ice class IB or IC a ship, to which ice class regulations 1985 (2.9.1985, No. 2575/85/307, as amended) apply, shall comply with the required minimum engine output as defined in section 3.2.1 of the ice class regulations 1985. For ease of reference, the provisions for ice classes IB and IC of section 3.2.1 of the ice class regulations 1985 are given in Annex II of these regulations.

In order to retain ice class IA Super or IA a ship, the keel of which has been laid or which has been at a similar stage of construction before 1 September 2003, shall comply with the requirements in section 3.2.2 above not later than 1 January in the year when twenty years have elapsed since the year the ship was delivered.
For IA Super without a bulb, compute C_1=f_1*(B*L)/(2*T/B+1)+1.84*(f_2*B+f_3*L+f_4*B*L) and C_2=3.52*(g_1+g_2*B)+g_3*(1+1.2*T/B)*B^2/sqrt(L).
For IA Super with a bulb, compute C_1=f_1*(B*L)/(2*T/B+1)+2.89*(f_2*B+f_3*L+f_4*B*L) and C_2=6.67*(g_1+g_2*B)+g_3*(1+1.2*T/B)*B^2/sqrt(L).

Coefficients f_1-f_4 and g_1-g_3 are given in Table 3-3. C_3 = 460 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_4 = 18.7 kg/(m^2*s^2), C_5 = 825 kg/s^2. If the value of the term ((L*T)/B^2)^3 is less than 5, the value 5 shall be used; if the value is more than 20, the value 20 shall be used. Section 3.2.4 applies to IA Super or IA ships whose keel was laid or which were at a similar stage of construction before 1 September 2003. Table 3-3 values: f1=10.3 N/m2, f2=45.8 N/m, f3=2.94 N/m, f4=5.8 N/m2, g1=1530 N, g2=170 N/m, g3=400 N/m1.5.

For an individual ship, in lieu of the Ke or RCH values defined in sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.3, the use of Ke or RCH values based on more precise calculations or values based on model tests may be approved. Such approval will be given on the understanding that it can be revoked if experience of the ship's performance provides grounds for this in practice.

Direct analysis may be substituted for the formulae and values given in this section if they are deemed by the Administration or the classification society to be invalid or inapplicable for a given structural arrangement or detail. Otherwise, direct analysis is not to be used as an alternative to the analytical procedures prescribed by the explicit requirements in sections 4.3 - 4.5.

Direct analyses are to be carried out using the load patch defined in section 4.2 (p, h and la). The pressure to be used is 1.8p where p is determined according to 4.2.2. The load patch must be applied at locations where the capacity of the structure under the combined effects of bending and shear is minimised. In particular, the structure must be checked with a load centred at the UIWL, 0.5h0 below the LIWL, and positioned at several vertical locations in between. Several horizontal locations shall also be checked, especially the locations centred at the mid-span or -spacing. Furthermore, if the load length la cannot be determined directly from the arrangement of the structure, several values of la shall be checked using corresponding values for ca.

The acceptance criterion for designs is that the combined stresses from bending and shear, when using the von Mises yield criterion, are lower than the yield point sigmay. When the direct calculation is based on beam theory, the allowable shear stress must be no larger than 0.9*tauy, where tauy = sigmay/sqrt3.
If scantlings derived from these regulations are less than those required by the classification society for a ship that has not been ice strengthened, the latter shall be used.

NB3. The requirements for the section modulus and shear area of the frames, stringers and web frames in 4.4, 4.5 and 4.6 are in accordance with the effective member cross section. For cases where the member is not normal to the plating, the section properties must be calculated in accordance with the appropriate classification society rules for the ship in question.
L shall be taken as the ship's rule length used by the classification society.

An ice-strengthened ship is assumed to operate in open sea conditions corresponding to a level ice thickness not exceeding hi. The design ice load height (h) of the area actually under ice pressure at any particular point of time is, however, assumed to be only a fraction of the ice thickness. The values for hi and h are given in Table 4-1. Table 4-1 values (ice class: hi, h in metres): IA Super: 1.0, 0.35; IA: 0.8, 0.30; IB: 0.6, 0.25; IC: 0.4, 0.22.

The design ice pressure is determined by the formula p = c_d*c_p*c_a*p_0 [MPa] (4.1), where c_d is a factor which takes account of the influence of the size and engine output of the ship. The maximum value is c_d = 1. It is calculated using c_d = (a*k + b)/1000 (4.2).

Use displacement_Delta_t at maximum ice-class draught. total_propulsion_power_for_scantlings_kW shall include the main engine and every additional propulsion power source and shall be stated on the shell expansion drawing. Select c_p from Table 4-3. Compute c_a = clamp(l_a/l_0, 0.35, 1.0), where l_0 = 0.6 m. Use nominal_ice_pressure_p_0_MPa = 5.6.

IF iceClass = 'IA Super', THEN forefoot_shell_strengthening_status = bow_region_equivalent for the specified five-main-frame-spacing extent. IF iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA'} AND open_water_service_speed_kn >= 18, THEN upper_bow_ice_belt_strengthening_status = midbody_equivalent for the area from the ice-belt upper limit to 2 m above it and at least 0.2*L aft of the forward perpendicular. sidescuttle_in_ice_belt = false. IF weather_deck_below_ice_belt_upper_limit = true, THEN bulwark_strength_status and freeing_port_strength_status shall meet the ice-belt shell requirement. The lower-speed model-test sentence is advisory and is not encoded as a mandatory constraint.

For transverse framing, the thickness of the shell plating shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(f_1*p_pl/sigma_y) + t_c [mm] (4.5). For longitudinal framing, the thickness shall be determined by t = 667*s*sqrt(p/(f_2*sigma_y)) + t_c [mm] (4.6).

f_2 = 0.4/(h/s) + 0.6 where h/s <= 1; f_2 = 1.4 - 0.4*(h/s) where 1 <= h/s <= 1.8. Here h is as given in section 4.2.1 and sigma_y is the yield stress of the material [N/mm^2]. Use sigma_y = 235 N/mm^2 for normal-strength hull structural steel and sigma_y = 315 N/mm^2 or higher for high-strength hull structural steel. If steels with different yield stress are used, actual accepted values may be substituted. The abrasion and corrosion increment t_c shall normally be 2 mm; a lower approved value may be used for a suitable maintained special surface coating.

Set the vertical extent of framing ice strengthening from Table 4-6. IF upper_bow_ice_belt_required = true, THEN framing_ice_strengthening_upper_extent >= upper_bow_ice_belt_top. IF extension_beyond_adjacent_deck_or_tank_boundary_mm <= 250, THEN termination_at_that_boundary is permitted. Table 4-6 values: IA Super framing above UIWL 1.2 m; below LIWL bow down to tank top or below top of floors, midbody 2.0 m, stern 1.6 m. IA, IB and IC framing above UIWL 1.0 m; below LIWL bow 1.6 m, midbody 1.3 m, stern 1.0 m.

Compute m_t = 7*m_0/(7 - 5*h/l), Z_cm3 = p_MPa*s_m*h_m*l_m/(m_t*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6, and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*1.2*p_MPa*h_m*s_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4. Select m_0 from Table 4-7 for the frame boundary condition. Table 4-7 m0 values: bulk carrier frames with top wing tanks 7; frames from tank top to main deck of a single-decked vessel 6; continuous frames between several decks or stringers 5.7; frames between two decks only 5.
Where less than 15% of the span, l, of the frame is situated within the ice-strengthening zone for frames as defined in 4.4.1, ordinary frame scantlings may be used.

The upper end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where a frame terminates above a deck or a stringer which is situated at or above the upper limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the part above the deck or stringer may have the scantlings required by the classification society for an non ice-strengthened ship and the upper end of an intermediate frame may be connected to the adjacent frames by a horizontal member with the same scantlings as the main frame.

The lower end of the strengthened part of a main frame and of an intermediate ice frame shall be attached to a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or an ice stringer (section 4.5). Where an intermediate frame terminates below a deck, top or bottom plating of a tank, tank top or ice stringer which is situated at or below the lower limit of the ice belt (section 4.3.1), the lower end may be connected to the adjacent main frames by a horizontal member of the same scantlings as the main frames. Note that the main frames below the lower edge of the ice belt must be ice strengthened, see 4.4.1.

Compute f_4 = 1 - 0.2*h/s, Z_cm3 = f_4*p_MPa*h_m*l_m^2/(4*m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6, and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*f_4*2.16*p_MPa*h_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4. Use m = 13.3 for a continuous beam with brackets unless the actual end field requires a smaller factor. Exclude bracket area from actual_frame_shear_area.

Within the ice-strengthened area, all frames shall be effectively attached to all of the supporting structures. A longitudinal frame shall be attached by brackets to all supporting web frames and bulkheads. When a transversal frame terminates at a stringer or deck, a bracket or similar construction must be fitted. When a frame is running through the supporting structure, both sides of the web plate of the frame must be connected to the structure (by direct welding, collar plate or lug). When a bracket is installed, it must have at least the same thickness as the web plate of the frame and the edge must be appropriately stiffened against buckling.
The frames shall be attached to the shell by a double continuous weld. No scalloping is allowed (except when crossing shell plate butts).

The web thickness of the frames shall be at least the maximum of: h_w*sqrt(sigma_y)/C, where C = 805 for profiles and C = 282 for flat bars; half of the net shell-plating thickness t - t_c; and 9 mm. Where a deck, tank top, tank bottom or bulkhead is used in lieu of a frame, its plate thickness shall be calculated in the same way using the adjacent frame height h_w and C = 805.

IF frame_asymmetrical = true OR frame_web_angle_to_shell_deg < 90, THEN antitripping_support_spacing_mm <= 1300. IF frame_span_m > 4, THEN antitripping_support_scope = 'all regions/all ice classes'. IF frame_span_m <= 4, THEN required scope is all regions for IA Super, bow and midbody for IA, and bow for IB or IC. An alternative arrangement is acceptable only when equivalent_support_status_by_direct_calculation = demonstrated.

Set design_line_load_MN_m = max(p_MPa*h_m, 0.15). Compute Z_cm3 = 0.9*1.8*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m^2/(m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^6 and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*0.9*1.8*1.2*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*10^4, with m selected under 4.4.3.

Set design_line_load_MN_m = max(p_MPa*h_m, 0.15) and outside_ice_belt_factor = 1 - h_s_m/l_s_m. Compute Z_cm3 = 0.80*1.8*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m^2/(m*sigma_y_N_mm2)*outside_ice_belt_factor*10^6 and A_cm2 = sqrt(3)*0.80*1.8*1.2*design_line_load_MN_m*l_m/(2*sigma_y_N_mm2)*outside_ice_belt_factor*10^4.

Narrow deck strips abreast of hatches and serving as ice stringers shall comply with the section modulus and shear area requirements given in 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 respectively. In the case of very long hatches, the classification society may permit the product p* h to be given a value of less than 0.15 but in no case less than 0.10.
Regard shall be paid to the deflection of the ship's sides due to ice pressure with respect to very long (more than B/2) hatch openings, when designing weatherdeck hatch covers and their fittings.

The ice load transferred to a web frame from an ice stringer or from longitudinal framing shall be F = f_12*p*h*S [MN] (4.15). When calculating c_a, use l_a = 2*S. If p*h is less than 0.15 MN/m, use 0.15 MN/m. Use f_12 = 1.8.
If the supported stringer is outside the ice belt, the force F shall be multiplied by (1- hs/ls), where hs and ls shall be as defined in section 4.5.2.
Compute M_MNm = 0.193*F_MN*L_m and A_a_cm2 = A_f_cm2 + A_w_cm2. Then compute Z_cm3 = (M_MNm/sigma_y_N_mm2)*sqrt(1/(1 - (gamma*A_required_cm2/A_a_cm2)^2))*10^6, with gamma selected from Table 4-8.
The stem and the part of a blunt bow defined above shall be supported by floors or brackets spaced no more than 0.6 m apart and with a thickness of at least half the plate thickness.
In order to avoid very high loads on propeller blade tips, the minimum distance between the propeller(s) and the hull (including stern frame) should be no less than h0 (see 4.2.1).
On twin and triple screw ships, the ice strengthening of the shell and framing shall be extended to the tank top 1.5 metres forward and aft of the side propellers.

The shafting and stern tubes of side propellers shall normally be enclosed within plated bossings. If detached struts are used, due consideration shall be taken of their design, strength and attachments to the hull.
The maximum service speed of the ship to be used in these calculations shall not be given a value lower than: IA Super 20 knots, IA 18 knots, IB 16 knots, IC 14 knots.

For ice classes IA and IA Super, the rudder (the rudder stock and the upper part of the rudder) shall be protected from direct contact with intact ice by an ice knife that extends below the LIWL, if practicable (or equivalent means).

For ice classes IA and IA Super, due regard shall be paid to the large loads that arise when the rudder is forced out of the midship position when sailing astern in ice or into ice ridges. Suitable arrangements such as rudder stoppers shall be installed to absorb such loads.

hydraulic_rudder_relief_valve_present = true. Steering-gear components shall have dimensioning_analysis_status = compliant for the applicable loads and required rudder-stock diameter without exceeding yield stress.

The propulsion-machinery rule applies when iceClass IN {'IA Super','IA','IB','IC'} and propeller_type IN {'open','ducted'} and pitch_type IN {'controllable','fixed'}. The design-load scope shall cover normal service-life propeller/ice loads, including FP reversal loads, and shall record that stopped-propeller dragging and radial ice entry into a turned azimuthing thruster are outside the prescribed load-model scope.

The regulations also apply to azimuthing and fixed thrusters for main propulsion, taking consideration of loads resulting from propeller/ice interaction and loads on the thruster body/ice interaction. The given azimuthing thruster body loads are the expected ice loads for the ship's service life under normal operational conditions. The local strength of the thruster body shall be sufficient to withstand local ice pressure when the thruster body is designed for extreme loads.

For every seawater-exposed propeller, hub, or thruster-body material: elongation_test_percent >= 15 using gauge_length = 5*specimen_diameter. Unless material_type is bronze or austenitic steel, Charpy_V_test_count = 3 and average_impact_energy_J >= 20 at test_temperature_degC = -10. For nodular cast iron, average_impact_energy_J >= 10 at -10 deg C.

Seawater-temperature-exposed components shall use steel or another ductile material. For the listed shafts, bolts, CP mechanisms, and connecting components, Charpy_V_test_count = 3 and average_impact_energy_J >= 20 at -10 deg C, except for surface-hardened bearings and gear teeth. For permitted ferritic nodular cast-iron parts other than bolts, average_impact_energy_J >= 10 at -10 deg C.

If the highest point of the propeller is not at a depth of at least hi below the water surface when the ship is in ballast condition, the propulsion system shall be designed according to ice class IA for ice classes IB and IC.

Fb is the maximum force experienced during the lifetime of a ship that bends a propeller blade backwards when the propeller mills an ice block while rotating ahead. Ff is the maximum force experienced during the lifetime of a ship that bends a propeller blade forwards when the propeller mills an ice block while rotating ahead. Fb and Ff originate from different propeller/ice interaction phenomena, and do not occur simultaneously. Hence, they are to be applied to one blade separately.
Load cases 1-4 must be covered, as given in Table 6-4 below, for CP and FP propellers. To obtain blade ice loads for a reversing propeller, load case 5 must also be covered for FP propellers.

where k is the shape parameter of the spectrum, Nice is the number of load cycles in the spectrum, and Fice is the random variable for ice loads on the blade, 0 <= Fice <= (Fice)max. The shape parameter k=0.75 shall be used for the ice force distribution of an open propeller and the shape parameter k=1.0 for that of a ducted propeller blade.

The number of load cycles per propeller blade in the load spectrum shall be N_ice = k_1*k_2*k_3*N_class*n_n (6.14), where N_class is given in Table 6-6 and the propeller location factor k_1 is given in Table 6-7.

The submersion factor k_2 is determined as follows: k_2 = 0.8 - f when f < 0; k_2 = 0.8 - 0.4*f when 0 <= f <= 1; k_2 = 0.6 - 0.2*f when 1 < f <= 2.5; and k_2 = 0.1 when f > 2.5 (6.15). The immersion function is f = (h_0 - H_ice)/(D/2) - 1 (6.16).

For components that are subject to loads resulting from propeller/ice interaction with all the propeller blades, the number of load cycles (Nice) must be multiplied by the number of propeller blades (Z).

Compute T_f_kN = 1.1*F_f_kN and T_b_kN = 1.1*F_b_kN. Compute forward_design_thrust_T_r_kN = hydrodynamic_bollard_thrust_T_kN + 2.2*T_f_kN and backward_design_thrust_T_r_kN = 1.5*T_b_kN. Set design_thrust_T_r_kN = max(forward_design_thrust_T_r_kN, backward_design_thrust_T_r_kN) for both directions.
If the hydrodynamic bollard thrust, T, is not known, it must be taken as given in Table 6-8.
n is the rotational propeller speed at MCR in bollard condition. If unknown, n must be attributed a value in accordance with Table 6-9.

For CP propellers, the propeller pitch, P0.7 shall correspond to MCR in bollard condition. If not known, P0.7 shall have a value equal to 0.7*P0.7n, where P0.7n is the propeller pitch at MCR in free running condition.
Set propeller_speed_MCR_bollard_rpm to the known rotational propeller speed at MCR in bollard condition; otherwise select propeller_speed_MCR_bollard_rpm from Table 6-9.

For CP propellers, the propeller pitch, P0.7 shall correspond to MCR in bollard condition. If not known, P0.7 shall have a value equal to 0.7*P0.7n, where P0.7n is the propeller pitch at MCR in free running condition.
All the torques and the inertia moments shall be reduced to the rotation speed of the component being examined.
If the maximum torque, Qemax, is unknown, it shall be accorded the value given in Table 6-10.

If there is first blade order torsional resonance in the operational speed range or in the range 20% above and 20% below the maximum operating speed (bollard condition), the design torque Q_peak of the shaft component shall be determined by means of torsional vibration analysis, using frequency domain calculation as one of the two alternative methods.
Time domain calculations shall be calculated for the MCR condition, MCR bollard conditions and for blade order resonant rotational speeds so that the resonant vibration responses can be obtained.

The load sequence given in this chapter, for a case where a propeller is milling an ice block, shall be used for the strength evaluation of the propulsion line. The given load sequence is not intended for propulsion system stalling analyses.

The following load cases are intended to reflect the operational loads on the propulsion system, when the propeller interacts with ice, and the respective reaction of the complete system. The ice impact and system response causes loads in the individual shaft line components. The ice torque Qmax may be taken as a constant value in the complete speed range. When considerations at specific shaft speeds are performed, a relevant Qmax may be calculated using the relevant speed according to section 6.5.3.

Diesel engine plants without an elastic coupling shall be calculated at the least favourable phase angle for ice versus engine excitation, when calculated in the time domain. The engine firing pulses shall be included in the calculations and their standard steady state harmonics can be used.
If there is a blade order resonance just above the MCR speed, calculations shall cover rotational speeds up to 105% of the MCR speed.

For transient shaft-line analysis in the time domain, the propeller ice torque excitation is a sequence of half-sine blade impacts whose frequency follows propeller rotational speed. The torque from one blade impact is Q(phi) = C_q*Q_max*sin(phi*(180/alpha_i)) for 0 <= phi <= alpha_i plus integer revolutions (6.29); otherwise Q(phi) = 0 (6.30). C_q and alpha_i are given in Table 6-11.

If a speed drop occurs until the main engine is at a standstill, this indicates that the engine may not be sufficiently powered for the intended service task. For the consideration of loads, the maximum occurring torque during the speed drop process must be used.
If the time-domain response does not already include the engine and propeller mean torques, compute Q_peak = Q_emax + Q_rtd.

For frequency-domain calculations, blade-order and twice-blade-order excitation may be used. The propeller ice torque is Q_F(phi) = Q_max*(C_q0 + C_q1*sin(Z*E_0*phi + alpha_1) + C_q2*sin(2*Z*E_0*phi + alpha_2)) [kNm] (6.33). The coefficients and excitation cases are given in Table 6-12.
For each frequency-domain excitation case, compute Q_peak = Q_emax + Q_vib + (Q_max_n*C_q0)*(I_e/I_t) + Q_rf1 + Q_rf2 and scale all torque values to the component shaft speed.

For time-domain torsional analysis, the model shall include propeller ice excitation, other relevant excitations, prime-mover mean torque, hydrodynamic propeller mean torque, damping, and variation of phase between ice and prime-mover excitations. The analysis shall cover MCR, MCR bollard, and resonant speeds. For frequency-domain analysis, derive Fourier components from the continuous half-sine sequence and include first- and second-order blade excitation components.

Determine blade_failure_load_F_ex_kN by an approved non-linear stress analysis OR compute F_ex = 300*c*t^2*sigma_ref1/(0.8*D - 2*r), where sigma_ref1 = 0.6*sigma_0.2 + 0.4*sigma_u. Apply the load at 0.8R in the weakest direction. blade_failure_status = failed IF blade_tip_offset_m > 0.10*propeller_diameter_m.
Compute C_spex = max(0.3, 0.7*(1 - ((4*EAR)/Z)^3)) and Q_sex_kNm = max(C_LE0.8, 0.8*C_TE0.8)*C_spex*F_ex_kN, unless an appropriate stress analysis directly determines the maximum spindle torque.

Csp is a non-dimensional parameter taking account of the spindle arm Cfex is a non-dimensional parameter taking account of the reduction of the blade failure force at the location of the maximum spindle torque. The strength of the propulsion line shall be designed according to the pyramid strength principle. This means that the loss of the propeller blade shall not cause any significant damage to other propeller shaft line components.

Blade stresses shall be calculated for the design loads in section 6.5.1. Finite element analysis shall be used for final approval of all propellers. The simplified root-area estimate is sigma_st = C_1*M_BL/(100*c*t^2) [MPa] (6.38).

Require sigma_ref2_MPa/sigma_st_MPa >= 1.3, where sigma_ref2_MPa = min(0.7*sigma_u_MPa, 0.6*sigma_0_2_MPa + 0.4*sigma_u_MPa). If finite_element_analysis_used = true, stress_measure = von_Mises. Fatigue verification shall use the service-life load distribution and the material S-N curve to calculate an equivalent stress producing the same fatigue damage, normalized to 10^8 cycles, and shall satisfy the section 6.6.2.4 acceptability criterion.
The type of the SN-curve shall be selected to correspond with the material properties of the blade. If the SN-curve is unknown, the two slope SN curve shall be used.
The coefficients C1, C2, C3, and C4 are given in Table 6-14. The applicable range of Nice for calculating rho is 5x106 <= Nice <= 108.

At every blade location, require sigma_fl/sigma_fat >= 1.5. If actual reduction factors are unavailable, use gamma_e1*gamma_e2 = 0.67, gamma_v = 0.75, and gamma_m = 0.75. The shafts and shafting components, such as the thrust and stern tube bearings, couplings, flanges and sealings, shall be designed to withstand the propeller/ice interaction loads as given in section 6.5. The safety factor must be at least 1.3 against yielding for extreme operational loads, 1.5 for fatigue loads and 1.0 against yielding for the blade failure load.

The ultimate load resulting from total blade failure, as defined in section 6.5.4 should not cause yielding in shafts and shaft components. The loading shall consist of the combined axial, bending, and torsion loads, wherever this is significant. The minimum safety factor against yielding must be 1.0 for bending and torsional stresses.

The steering mechanism, the fitting of the unit, and the body of the thruster shall be designed to withstand the plastic bending of a blade without damage. The loss of a blade must be taken into account for the propeller blade orientation causing the maximum load on the component being studied. Top-down blade orientation typically places the maximum bending loads on the thruster body.

The thruster must withstand the loads occurring when the design ice block defined in Table 6-3 impacts on the thruster body when the ship is sailing at a typical ice operating speed. Load cases for impact loads are given in Table 6-16. The contact geometry is estimated to be hemispherical in shape. If the actual contact geometry differs from the shape of the hemisphere, a sphere radius must be estimated so that the growth of the contact area as a function of penetration of ice corresponds as closely as possible to the actual geometrical shape penetration.
For impacts on non-hemispherical areas, such as the impact on the nozzle, the equivalent impact sphere radius must be estimated using the equation below.

The stresses on the thruster must be calculated for the extreme once-in-a-lifetime loads described in section 6.6.5. The nominal von Mises stresses on the thruster body must have a safety margin of 1.3 against the yielding strength of the material. At areas of local stress concentrations, stresses must have a safety margin of 1.0 against yielding. The slewing bearing, bolt connections and other components must be able to maintain operability without incurring damage that requires repair when subject to the loads given in sections 6.6.5.2 and 6.6.5.3 multiplied by a safety factor of 1.3.

Evaluating the global vibratory behavior of the thruster body is important, if the first blade order excitations are in the same frequency range with the thruster global modes of vibration, which occur when the propeller rotational speeds are in the high power range of the propulsion line. This evaluation is mandatory and it must be shown that there is either no global first blade order resonance at high operational propeller speeds (above 50% of maximum power) or that the structure is designed to withstand vibratory loads during resonance above 50% of maximum power.

When estimating thruster global natural frequencies in the longitudinal and transverse direction, the damping and added mass due to water must be taken into account. In addition to this, the effect of ship attachment stiffness must be modelled.

As an alternative to sections 6.5 and 6.6, a comprehensive design study may be performed to the satisfaction of the Administration or the classification society in question. The study must be based on the ice conditions given for different ice classes in section 6.3. It must include both fatigue and maximum load design calculations and fulfil the pyramid strength principle, as given in section 6.6.1.

The analysis must confirm that all components transmitting random (occasional) forces, excluding propeller blade, are not subjected to stress levels in excess of the yield stress of the component material, with a reasonable safety margin.
A vibration analysis must be performed and demonstrate that the overall dynamic system is free of the harmful torsional resonances resulting from propeller/ice interaction.

The length LUI is the distance, in m, measured horizontally from the fore side of the stem at the intersection with the upper ice waterline (UIWL) to the after side of the rudder post, or the centre of the rudder stock if there is no rudder post. LUI is not to be less than 96%, and need not be greater than 97%, of the extreme length of the upper ice waterline (UIWL) measured horizontally from the fore side of the stem. In ships with unusual stern and bow arrangement the length LUI will be specially considered.

The ship displacement DUI is the displacement, in kt, of the ship corresponding to the upper ice waterline (UIWL). Where multiple waterlines are used for determining the UIWL, the displacement is to be determined from the waterline corresponding to the greatest displacement.
The boundary between the bottom and lower regions is to be taken at the point where the shell is inclined 7 deg from horizontal.

(iii) Within the Bow area of all Polar Class ships, and within the Bow Intermediate Icebelt area of Polar Class PC6 and PC7, the ice load parameters are functions of the actual bow shape. The required minimum shell plate thickness, t, is given by: t = tnet + ts [mm] where tnet = plate thickness required to resist ice loads according to I2.4.2 [mm] ts = corrosion and abrasion allowance according to I2.11 [mm] The thickness of shell plating required to resist the design ice load, tnet, depends on the orientation of the framing.
For transversely-framed plating (Omega >= 70 deg), including bottom plating in hull areas BI_b, M_b and S_b, t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)/(1 + s/(2*b)) [mm].

For longitudinally-framed plating (Omega <= 20 deg) when b >= s, t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)/(1 + s/(2*l)) [mm]. When b < s, t_net = 500*s*sqrt((AF*PPF_p*P_avg)/sigma_y)*sqrt(2*b/s - (b/s)^2)/(1 + s/(2*l)) [mm].
In the case of obliquely-framed plating (70 deg > Omega > 20 deg), linear interpolation is to be used.

The strength of a framing member is dependent upon the fixity that is provided at its supports. Fixity can be assumed where framing members are either continuous through the support or attached to a supporting section with a connection bracket. In other cases, simple support is to be assumed unless the connection can be demonstrated to provide significant rotational restraint. Fixity is to be ensured at the support of any framing which terminates within an ice-strengthened area.

When calculating the section modulus and shear area of a framing member, net thicknesses of the web, flange (if fitted) and attached shell plating are to be used. The shear area of a framing member may include that material contained over the full depth of the member, i.e. web area including portion of flange, if fitted, but excluding attached shell plating.

When the local-frame area exceeds the attached-plate-flange area, z_na = (100*A_fn + h_w*t_wn - 1000*t_pn*s)/(2*t_wn) [mm]. The net effective plastic section modulus is Z_p = t_pn*s*(z_na + t_pn/2)*sin(phi_w) + (((h_w - z_na)^2 + z_na^2)*t_wn*sin(phi_w))/2000 + A_fn*((h_fc - z_na)*sin(phi_w) - b_w*cos(phi_w))/10 [cm^3]. For oblique framing (70 deg > Omega > 20 deg), use linear interpolation.

The local frames in bottom structures (i.e. hull areas BIb, Mb and Sb) and transverse local frames in side structures are to be dimensioned such that the combined effects of shear and bending do not exceed the plastic strength of the member. The plastic strength is defined by the magnitude of midspan load that causes the development of a plastic collapse mechanism. For bottom structure the patch load shall be applied with the dimension (b) parallel with the frame direction.

The actual net effective shear area A_w shall satisfy A_w >= A_t, where A_t = 100^2*0.5*LL*s*(AF*PPF*P_avg)/(0.577*sigma_y) [cm^2]. LL is the lesser of frame span a and load-patch height b; the remaining variables are defined in I2.6.2.

Longitudinal local frames in side structures are to be dimensioned such that the combined effects of shear and bending do not exceed the plastic strength of the member. The plastic strength is defined by the magnitude of midspan load that causes the development of a plastic collapse mechanism.

The actual net effective shear area A_w shall satisfy A_w >= A_L, where A_L = 100^2*(AF*PPF_s*P_avg)*0.5*b_1*a/(0.577*sigma_y) [cm^2], b_1 = k_o*b_2, k_o = 1 - 0.3/b_prime, b_prime = b/s, and b_2 = b*(1 - 0.25*b_prime) when b_prime < 2, otherwise b_2 = s.

Web frames and load-carrying stringers are to be designed to withstand the ice load patch as defined in I2.3. The load patch is to be applied at locations where the capacity of these members under the combined effects of bending and shear is minimised.
To prevent local web buckling, h_w/t_wn <= 282/sqrt(sigma_y) for flat-bar sections and h_w/t_wn <= 805/sqrt(sigma_y) for bulb, tee and angle sections.

In addition, the net web thickness shall satisfy t_wn >= 0.35*t_pn*sqrt(sigma_y/235), where sigma_y is the minimum upper yield stress of the shell plate and t_pn is the net shell-plate thickness in way of the framing member.
(i) The flange width, bf [mm], is not to be less than five times the net thickness of the web, twn.

IF ship_operates_in_ice_covered_waters = true OR direct_evacuation_onto_ice_applicable = true, THEN safe_evacuation_means_present = true AND survival_equipment_deployment_approval_status = approved.
IF added_life_saving_device_requires_power = true, THEN device_power_source_independent_of_main_power = true.
IF ship_type = passenger_ship, THEN every person on board shall have one properly sized immersion suit OR one thermal protective aid.
IF immersion_suit_required = true, THEN immersion_suit_type = insulated.
IF extended_darkness_operation = true, THEN every lifeboat shall have an assigned searchlight with continuous_use_suitability_status = approved.
Every lifeboat_type shall be in {'partially enclosed','totally enclosed'}.
IF abandonment_onto_ice_or_land_potential = true, THEN group_survival_equipment_carried = true OR normal_life_saving_equivalent_functionality_approval_status = approved.
IF personal_or_group_survival_equipment_required = true, THEN available_survival_equipment_capacity >= ceil(persons_on_board * 1.10) AND storage_accessibility_status = accessible.
Every group-survival-equipment container shall have ice_mobility_test_status = passed AND flotation_test_status = passed.

IF additional_equipment_carried_in_survival_craft = true, THEN survival_craft_available_capacity >= persons_capacity_requirement + additional_equipment_capacity_requirement AND launching_appliance_capacity >= loaded_survival_craft_requirement.
Every passenger shall have personal-survival-equipment instruction_status = completed; every crew member shall have personal_and_group_survival_equipment_training_status = completed.
available_emergency_ration_person_days >= persons_on_board * maximum_expected_rescue_time_days.
ice_information_receiver_present = true AND ice_information_display_present = true AND displayed_ice_information_status = current for the operating area.
IF construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND ship_ice_strengthened = true, THEN independent_echo_sounding_device_count >= 2 OR (echo_sounding_device_count >= 1 AND independent_transducer_count >= 2).

encoding_pattern: Cross-regulation compliance and conditional status constraint
normalized_requirement: SOLAS_V_22_1_9_4_compliance_status = compliant AND, where required by bridge configuration, clear_view_astern_status = compliant.
IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN every required navigation or communication antenna shall have ice_accumulation_prevention_means_present = true.
IF required_sensor_projects_below_hull = true, THEN sensor_ice_protection_present = true.
IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN bridge_wings_enclosed = true OR bridge_wing_protection_design_status = approved.
non_magnetic_heading_means_count >= 2; the two means shall be independent and each shall be connected to main_power and emergency_power.
IF planned_or_actual_latitude_deg > 80, THEN GNSS_compass_or_equivalent_count >= 1 AND connected_to_main_power = true AND connected_to_emergency_power = true.

IF solely_24_hour_daylight_operation = false, THEN (bridge_controlled_rotatable_narrow_beam_searchlight_count >= 2 AND searchlight_coverage_arc_deg >= 360) OR alternate_visual_ice_detection_means_approval_status = approved.

IF icebreaker_escort_operation = true, THEN manually_initiated_flashing_red_stopped_light_present = true, light_visible_from_astern = true, visibility_range_nm >= 2, and COLREG_stern_light_arc_compliance_status = compliant.
For every point on the intended operating route, ship_to_ship_communication_available = true AND ship_to_shore_communication_available = true using voice and/or data.
two_way_on_scene_communication_present = true AND SAR_coordination_communication_present = true AND aeronautical_frequency_capability_present = true.
telemedical_assistance_communication_equipment_present = true.
Every mandatory survival-craft communication device shall have demonstrated_operating_duration_days >= maximum_expected_rescue_time_days AND duration_test_status = passed.
IF ship_provides_icebreaking_escort = true, THEN astern_facing_sound_signaling_system_present = true AND International_Code_of_Signals_compliance_status = compliant.
SAR_communication_capability shall include rescue_coordination_centre_voice_or_data = true AND aircraft_voice_frequency_support_MHz containing both 121.5 and 123.1.
TMAS_two_way_voice_capability = true AND TMAS_two_way_data_capability = true.

IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN every released rescue boat and lifeboat shall carry at least one ship-to-shore distress-alert device, one location-signal device, and one on-scene transmit/receive communication device.
IF ship_operates_in_low_air_temperature = true, THEN every other survival craft shall carry at least one location-signal device and one on-scene transmit/receive communication device.

battery_life_management_procedure_present = true AND procedure_implementation_status = active AND every mandatory survival-craft communication device shall remain available for maximum_expected_rescue_time_days.
voyage_plan_present = true AND every identified_intended_voyage_hazard shall be addressed by the voyage plan.

The polar-route planning record shall cover all nine clause 11.3 topics: PWOM procedures, hydrographic/navigation limitations, current ice/iceberg information, historical ice/temperature data, places of refuge, marine-mammal measures, routing/speed/VTS information, protected areas, and remoteness from SAR.

Required polar training level shall be derived from ice_condition, ship_type, and crew_role according to the clause 12.3.1 matrix, and each applicable crew member shall have a valid matching STCW qualification.

IF alternate_qualified_person_used = true, THEN administration_permission_status = approved and all five conditions in clause 12.3.2 shall be satisfied, including STCW II/2 and A-II/2 certification, advanced polar training, watch coverage, rest compliance, and the condition-specific basic-training safeguards for designated officers.
Every crew member shall have PWOM_familiarization_status = completed for all procedures and equipment relevant to assigned_duties.
IF operating_area = Arctic_waters, THEN oil_or_oily_mixture_discharge_to_sea = false.
IF discharged_material_type IN {clean_ballast, segregated_ballast}, THEN clause_1_1_1_oil_discharge_prohibition_applicable = false.
IF ship_operates_in_polar_waters = true, THEN polar_operation_coverage shall be present in the applicable Oil Record Book, manuals, and oil or marine pollution emergency plan.

IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND aggregate_oil_fuel_capacity_m3 < 600 AND individual_oil_fuel_tank_capacity_m3 > 30, THEN oil_fuel_tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.
IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND ship_type != oil_tanker AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND cargo_tank_carries_oil = true, THEN cargo_tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.

IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND ship_type = oil_tanker AND deadweight_tonnes < 5000 AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01', THEN entire_cargo_tank_length_double_bottom_protection_status = compliant with MARPOL I/19.6.1 AND wing_tank_protection_status = compliant with MARPOL I/19.3.1 and I/19.6.2.

IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND tank_type IN {oil_residue_tank, oily_bilge_water_holding_tank} AND individual_tank_capacity_m3 > 30, THEN tank_outer_shell_separation_m >= 0.76.
IF operating_area = Arctic_waters, THEN NLS_or_NLS_mixture_discharge_to_sea = false.
IF ship_operates_in_polar_waters = true, THEN polar_operation_coverage shall be present in the applicable Cargo Record Book, Manual, and NLS or marine pollution emergency plan.

IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND carried_NLS_requires_type_3_tank = true AND cargo_tank_type = 3, THEN administration_carriage_approval_status = approved AND applicable_certificate_polar_operation_entry_present = true.

IF sewage_discharge_type = comminuted_and_disinfected, THEN MARPOL_IV_11_1_1_compliance_status = compliant AND distance_to_nearest_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm > 3; record distance from areas with ice_concentration_tenths > 1.

IF sewage_discharge_type = not_comminuted_or_disinfected, THEN MARPOL_IV_11_1_1_compliance_status = compliant AND distance_to_nearest_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm > 12; record distance from areas with ice_concentration_tenths > 1.

IF sewage_discharge_uses_treatment_plant = true, THEN sewage_treatment_plant_approval_status = approved, MARPOL_IV_9_1_1_or_9_2_1_certification_status = compliant, MARPOL_IV_11_1_2_discharge_status = compliant, and distances to land, ice shelf, fast ice, and ice concentration greater than 1/10 shall be recorded.
IF construction_date >= '2017-01-01' AND (ship_category IN {'A','B'} OR ship_type = passenger_ship), THEN sewage_discharge_to_sea = false UNLESS clause_4_2_1_3_compliance_status = compliant.

IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND ice_concentration_tenths > 1 AND extended_period_operation = true AND sewage_discharge_occurs = true, THEN approved_sewage_treatment_plant_used = true, MARPOL_IV_9_1_1_or_9_2_1_certification_status = compliant, and administration_discharge_approval_status = approved.

IF operating_area = Arctic_waters AND food_waste_discharge_to_sea = true, THEN distance_to_nearest_land_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm >= 12 and the distance from areas with ice_concentration_tenths > 1 shall be recorded.
IF food_waste_discharge_to_sea = true, THEN food_waste_comminuted_or_ground = true, required_screen_opening_mm <= 25, and contaminated_by_other_garbage = false.
food_waste_discharge_onto_ice = false AND animal_carcass_discharge = false.

Cargo-residue discharge is permitted only if residue_not_recoverable_by_common_methods = true, ship_en_route = true, harmful_substance_present = false, departure_and_destination_within_Arctic = true, route_remains_within_Arctic = true, adequate_reception_facilities_available = false, and distance_to_nearest_land_ice_shelf_or_fast_ice_nm >= 12; record distance from ice concentration greater than 1/10.

IF operating_area = Antarctic_area AND MARPOL_V_6_1_discharge = true, THEN distance_to_nearest_fast_ice_nm >= 12 and the distance from areas with ice_concentration_tenths > 1 shall be recorded; food_waste_discharge_onto_ice = false.
IF ship_operates_in_polar_waters = true, THEN polar_operation_coverage shall be present in the applicable Garbage Record Book, Garbage Management Plan, and garbage placards.
Polar Code chapter 9 applies only when SOLAS_chapter_I_certified = true.

chapter_9_1_applicable = true IF (ship_type = fishing_vessel AND length_overall_m >= 24) OR (ship_type = pleasure_yacht AND gross_tonnage >= 300 AND engaged_in_trade = false) OR (ship_type = cargo_ship AND 300 <= gross_tonnage < 500).
IF chapter_9_1_applicable = true, THEN current_navigation_information_receiving_capability = true AND current_ice_information_receiving_capability = true.
IF chapter_9_1_applicable = true, THEN every navigation equipment item shall have environmental_functionality_test_status = passed for the expected operating-area conditions.
Every heading-reference and position-fixing system shall have intended_area_suitability_approval_status = approved.
IF chapter_9_1_applicable = true, THEN ice_information_receiver_present = true, ice_information_display_present = true, and displayed_ice_information_status = current for the operating area.

IF ship_ice_strengthened = true AND construction_date >= '2026-01-01', THEN independent_echo_sounding_device_count >= 2 OR (echo_sounding_device_count >= 1 AND independent_transducer_count >= 2) OR administration_approved_equivalent_depth_sounding_device_present = true.
SOLAS_V_22_1_9_4_compliance_status = compliant AND clear_view_astern_status = compliant, OR administration_approved_equivalent_visibility_arrangement_present = true.
IF ice_accretion_likely = true, THEN every required navigation or communication antenna shall have ice_accumulation_prevention_means_present = true.
IF required_sensor_projects_below_hull = true, THEN sensor_ice_protection_present = true.

IF ship_category IN {'A','B'} AND construction_date >= '2026-01-01', THEN bridge_wings_enclosed = true OR bridge_wing_protection_design_status = approved OR administration_approved_equivalent_bridge_wing_protection_present = true.

encoding_pattern: Conditional qualified count and topology constraint
normalized_requirement: IF gross_tonnage >= 500, THEN non_magnetic_heading_means_count >= 2; the means shall be independent and each connected to main_power and emergency_power.
IF planned_or_actual_latitude_deg > 80, THEN GNSS_compass_or_equivalent_count >= 1 AND connected_to_main_power = true AND connected_to_emergency_power = true.
IF solely_24_hour_daylight_operation = false, THEN visual_ice_detection_illumination_means_count >= 2.
Polar Code chapter 11 applies only when SOLAS_chapter_I_certified = true.

IF ship_operates_in_polar_waters = true, THEN chapter_11_1_applicable = true when (ship_type = fishing_vessel AND length_overall_m >= 24) OR (ship_type = pleasure_yacht AND gross_tonnage >= 300 AND engaged_in_trade = false) OR (ship_type = cargo_ship AND 300 <= gross_tonnage < 500).
IF chapter_11_1_applicable = true, THEN voyage_plan_present = true and every intended_voyage_hazard shall have voyage_plan_coverage = true.

IF chapter_11_1_applicable = true, THEN the route planning record shall cover all nine clause 11-1.3 topics; if safety_management_system_implemented = false, documented_polar_operation_procedure_present shall be true.
